newsitem.title: USA: Two accused of insider trade in Kmart deal.
newsitem.headline: Two accused of insider trade in Kmart deal.

text.p: U.S. regulators filed a complaint in a Michigan U.S. district court accusing two men of insider trading, the Securities and Exchange Commission said Monday.

In its complaint, the SEC alleged in late 1992 Michael J. Garzoni, employed in the real estate department at Kmart Corp's Michigan headquarters, obtained confidential information concerning the sale of a company to a Kmart unit.

It alleged Garzoni obtained inside information about Intelligent Electronics Inc's sale of its BizMart Inc affiliate to OfficeMax Inc, at the time a subsidiary of Kmart, the SEC said. The complaint alleges Garzoni tipped
Mark Aronds, president of Network Group Inc, a Houston based commercial real estate brokerage firm, prior to the public announcement of the sale on December 4, 1992.

From November 16 to December 3, 1992 Aronds invested $176,677 in Intelligent Electronics common stock and call option contracts and later sold his securities for a total profit of $263,835, the SEC alleged.
SEC said it is seeking permanent injunctions against Aronds and Garzoni, as well as disgorgement of all illegal profits and penalties.
Garzoni is no longer employed by Kmart, SEC said, but did not know when he left. Aronds is the sole owner of Network Group Inc.
Kmart used Network to help market some of its surplus properties, the SEC said in its complaint.
Kmart said it terminated Garzoni in 1992.
The company filed a suit against Garzoni and Aronds earlier this year in Houston.

The discount store company has charged Garzoni, who marketed property that was closed by Kmart in Texas, and Aronds concocted non-competitive real estate deals in which Kmart received unfavorable terms or paid out commissions in fraudulent transactions.
Kmart seeks to recover $20 million in losses through the suit. "We intend to vigorously pursue our legal action," said company spokesman Robert Burton.
Kmart launched an internal investigation of fraud in its real estate department this year, and that probe continues, Burton added.
